body:
I think there are two things here:
1. We need some way to reliably save the cache when the application is suspended on Android
2. We probably need to overhaul our approach to caching since it was made long before we started multithreading pipeline compilation and likely could be improved to work much better with ubershaders

For future reference:
1. Section on pipeline cache here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/7366
2. See comments here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/80296

> We need some way to reliably save the cache when the application is suspended on Android

From what I understand, the place where `NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_PAUSED` is emitted (i.e. the `Java_org_godotengine_godot_GodotLib_onRendererPaused` function linked above) is as good as it gets in terms of reliably doing anything before the application is quietly terminated by the OS, but @godotengine/android might want to confirm that.

I also forgot to mention an important detail, which is that this issue is seemingly made much worse by the fact that the driver's own pipeline cache doesn't seem to be working well on certain[^1] devices. So losing out on our own pipeline cache leaves you with very expensive pipeline compilations every single run until you hit the threshold dictated by `rendering/rendering_device/pipeline_cache/save_chunk_size_mb`.

[^1]: Adreno by the looks of it, but I don't have other GPUs to test with myself.

I'm having a similar problem, not on Android but on a similar architecture that also does not usually "exit normally" :)

After activating verbose output, I found out that the existing PSO cache was being discarded at the very start, even if I put a small chunk size to make the project update it oftenly enough.

After some debugging, I noticed that the size of the blob was bigger than expected, probably related to a race condition.
It seems that it is even expected according to this comment:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/7ed0b6167618f9c8c5df87c7e83da6003c081368/drivers/vulkan/rendering_device_driver_vulkan.cpp#L4764

And well, if the blob size is bigger than what is written in the header, Godot will discard it.
I fixed on my side by replacing this line:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/7ed0b6167618f9c8c5df87c7e83da6003c081368/drivers/vulkan/rendering_device_driver_vulkan.cpp#L4699
With this one:
```uint32_t loaded_buffer_size = loaded_header->data_size;```

It bypasses the size check but also limits the size of the buffer, and from my tests with a mid-sized 3D game with many shaders, it seems to be working well.

The check might be a bit redundant as we also check the hash from the header with the generated hash from the data in the blob.

I'm not sure if I just hit a bug or it's something that is only affecting my private architecture, but I'll mention it just in case it helps! 🙌

PS: I didn't open an issue for this because it might not be one, it might be probably only happening on my Switch port.
